nv_red_rocks.name: Red Rocks
nv_red_rocks.note: One guide: October to early April best; others say spring/fall preferred, busy Sep-Apr, winter workable (56F highs), summer too hot; window is Oct-Apr (Sep and May fringe left out).

excluded.nv_icebox_canyon: shaded, cold canyon; a different season is likely and no source names it
excluded.nv_mt_wilson: high peak walls; no source says the same window
excluded.nv_windy_peak: high peak; no source says the same window

co_south_platte.name: South Platte
co_south_platte.note: No source names months for the South Platte; only season words (spring/fall) from generic Front Range pages, and elevations range from Elevenmile (8,192 ft, short season) to low Front Range crags.

ut_southeast_utah.name: Southeast Utah
ut_southeast_utah.note: Region spans desert crags, La Sal Mountains and Canyonlands; too varied for one window. Only Indian Creek has a month-naming source.

ut_indian_creek.note: Mountain Project commenters (2003, 2017): March through mid-May and mid-September through November; other sources agree on spring/fall, summer hot on south-facing walls, winter hit-or-miss.

co_nine_mile_bouldering.name: Nine Mile Bouldering
co_nine_mile_bouldering.note: Sources give season words only (spring and fall) or conflict (year-round; March into December); none names the months for Nine Mile Hill.

wi_devil_s_lake.name: Devil's Lake
wi_devil_s_lake.note: Only KAYA names months (Sep-Nov prime, Mar-Jun good); no independent second source found, other sources give only shoulder-season words.
